title: Expressions & like terms
examples: What is the difference between a term and a variable?
Can I combine terms that have different letters?
How do I know which terms are like terms?

explain.say: Today we are learning about algebraic expressions. You will learn to simplify them. First we need to know what a term is. A term is a single number or variable part of an expression.

draw.text: Terms are parts of an expression.

explain.say: Next we look at the coefficient. The coefficient is the number that multiplies the variable. For example in three x, three is the coefficient.
Like terms have the exact same variables and exponents. You can only add or subtract terms that are like terms. For example five y and two y are like terms.

items: Only like terms can be added/subtracted

explain.say: To simplify we collect all the like terms together. You just add or subtract the coefficients. Remember to keep the variable part the same.

faq.q: What is a variable in algebra?
faq.a: A variable is a letter that stands for an unknown number. It can represent any value in a problem.

faq.q: What is the coefficient of x squared in five x squared?
faq.a: The coefficient is the number five. It tells you how many x squared groups you have.
asks: How do I find the coefficient?
Is the number always the coefficient?

faq.q: Can I combine terms like three x and three y?
faq.a: No you cannot combine them. They are not like terms because they have different variables. You must leave them separate.
asks: Are x and y like terms?
Do the variables have to match?

faq.q: What do I do when I simplify an expression?
faq.a: You combine all the terms that are alike. You only add or subtract the numbers in front of the variables.
asks: How do I simplify an expression?
What is the goal of simplifying?

faq.q: What is the coefficient of a single variable term like seven a?
faq.a: The coefficient is the number seven. It is the multiplier for the variable a.
asks: What is the number in front of a?
Does the variable count as a coefficient?

facts: A term is a single part of an algebraic expression.
The coefficient is the numerical factor multiplied by a variable.
Like terms must have the exact same variables and exponents.
To simplify, you add or subtract the coefficients of like terms.

quiz.why: We combine the x terms: four x plus three x equals seven x. The y term has no other like terms, so it stays as two y.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you only subtracted the coefficients instead of adding them.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you multiplied the variables together instead of adding the coefficients.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you forgot to combine the x terms fully.

quiz.why: We combine the a terms: five a minus two a equals three a. The term with b is different and remains as ten b.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you added the coefficients when you should have subtracted them.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you incorrectly changed the variable from a to b.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you treated the term with b as a constant number.

quiz.why: We group the m terms: eight m minus five m equals three m. We group the n terms: three n minus one n equals two n.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you only combined the m terms and ignored the n terms.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you incorrectly cancelled out the n terms completely.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you added the coefficients of the m terms instead of subtracting them.
